The long-awaited start to the 2026 NFL regular season has finally arrived, and this year's Kickoff Game fittingly features a Super Bowl LX rematch.

The Patriots pay a visit to the defending champion Seahawks' Lumen Field, as is the season-opening tradition. New England aims to atone for February's frustrating 29-13 loss and therefore begin its quest for a second consecutive shot at a Lombardi Trophy in style.

The Pats were essentially dominated for the majority of the time the game was still winnable, but with a high-end coaching staff having had a full offseason to analyze what went awry, it's understandable why a closely contested rematch seems like the likeliest outcome. However, given the power of Seattle's 12th man and the Seahawks' talent level, it's certainly possible for New England to play much better this time around and still come up short.

Given the modest number of points the conventional spread is affording us, utilizing FanDuel's Alternate Spread feature seems prudent. As such, we're giving the Pats four additional points to work with and pushing past the key number of seven points in the process.

New England had the league's second-best average scoring margin on the road last regular season (+10.0 points), and the Patriots went 8-0 straight up when traveling while going 4-0 against the spread as a road underdog with an ATS +/- of +8.5 points.

Trying to run on the Seahawks is typically a grind, as evidenced by the stingy 3.5 yards per carry they allowed to running backs during the 2025 regular season. Yet, this is a bet that banks on volume as much as anything else, not to mention a potentially better overall performance by New England's offensive line with the help of lessons learned in last year's Super Bowl.

In games last regular season and postseason in which Stevenson logged double-digit carries, he went 5-3 to the 50+ rushing yards prop, and he hit that figure on eight occasions overall. Barner finished the regular campaign with career bests across his receiving line (52-519-6) and then closed out Seattle's title-winning run with four receptions for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Super Bowl.

Barner averaged a modest 30.5 receiving yards per game during the 2025 regular season, but even that figure is well beyond what we need Barner to do Wednesday. title: The SEC will vote to expel LSU. Here's why
description: Lane Kiffin and the Tigers could be without a conference soon.
fullText:
The SEC will vote to expel LSU. Here's why originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The SEC is fed up with Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers after their debacle signing pro football players to the team. On Tuesday, the conference filed an amendment to its federal lawsuit against LSU, Lane Kiffin, and other representatives. This amendment seeks the power to expel LSU from the conference.

To do so, a vote of two-thirds of all the presidents is required to end a school's tenure with the conference according to SEC rules. The SEC said in a statement, "The SEC and its member universities have the right to establish, through agreed-upon governance procedures, the rules under which they voluntarily compete and to expect those rules to be followed."

"Today's filing is necessary to defend that right and preserve the Conference's ability to govern competition among its members."

A meeting is set for Thursday, September 10 to "decide whether to terminate Louisiana State University ("LSU") as an SEC member institution pursuant to Section 3.1.5 of the SEC Constitution and Bylaws," per On3 Sports.

If this does not show how fed up the SEC is with Lane Kiffin and his antics, then nothing does. According to ESPN, the SEC's amended complaint mentioned Kiffin's comments after their 5110 landslide win over Clemson on Saturday; "Imagine if we had pro players." His comment shows how he neglects the ruling that players who have signed a pro contract cannot return to college.

"The consensus at the September 4 meeting was and continues to be that LSU's demonstrated lack of institutional control at the university level—including complete lack of control over Coach Kiffin's actions — and other conduct alleged herein that is inconsistent with the principles and purposes of the Conference as set forth in Section 1.2 of the Constitution, made it imperative for a meeting to be called to consider the termination of LSU's membership in the Conference pursuant," the complaint reads.

This could impact LSU's season in a way that has rarely been seen. A notable instance when a team was voted out of a conference was in February 2001 when Temple University was voted out of the Big East. The decision came because of how abysmal Temple's program was and the failure to consistently reach the 25,000-attendance benchmark. Temple did everything they could to remain in the Big East and ultimately reached a settlement to play in the league through the 2004 season.

At the end of that season, Temple's record was 30-126 overall and 14-80 in the Big East. They played independent for two years before playing in the Mid-American Conference in 2007. Shortly after their stint with the MAC, the Big East came crawling back after losing several members to the ACC and Big 12.

LSU may not be so lucky if they do get voted out of the SEC. Conferences have an image to uphold, whether that's competitive teams, academic standards, money, etc., and if a school does anything to alter that image, there will be repercussions. LSU may have to find that out the hard way.

The SEC is sending a clear message that they will not tolerate any deviation from its rules, and rightfully so. The whole world will be watching on Thursday to see LSU's fate.

title: LSU announces final decision on adding former NFL players
description: The biggest storyline in college football over the past few weeks has been LSU and head coach Lane Kiffin’s attempts to add multiple players to its roster who had signed NFL contracts and spent time with NFL teams this preseason. Now, LSU has made a final decision on that matter. With the looming threat of…
fullText:
The biggest storyline in college football over the past few weeks has been LSU and head coach Lane Kiffin's attempts to add multiple players to its roster who had signed NFL contracts and spent time with NFL teams this preseason. Now, LSU has made a final decision on that matter.

With the looming threat of expulsion from the SEC, the Tigers have made it clear that they will not add the players to the roster this season.

Heading into the 2026 season, LSU and Kiffin had been moving forward with plans to bring in at least three players who signed professional contracts this summer, including former Ole Miss players Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris.

Adding those players to the roster would break two separate league rules, as the SEC prohibits players from entering the conference after signing a professional contract while also restricting intraconference transfers outside of the designated transfer portal window.

However, a Baton Rouge judge has issued an order preventing both the NCAA and SEC from enforcing their restrictions related to eligibility, the transfer portal, and professional players returning to college football.

On Thursday last week, Judge William Jorden, out of Baton Rouge, Louisiana, ruled in favor of LSU by approving a preliminary injunction "that prohibits the NCAA and SEC from punishing any school" that fields former professional players. That would have paved the way for the players to potentially play in Saturday's game against Clemson.

Ultimately, LSU opted against adding the players to the roster for this game. However, the team only rostered 103 players for the game, allowing two open spots to potentially add Wright and Harris to the roster later in the season.

According to college football insider Pete Thamel of ESPN, LSU has announced a final decision on the matter by adding two additional players to the school's roster. This means that the team's roster is now full at 105 players, and Wright and Harris will not be able to be added to the roster this season.

"NEWS: LSU football is adding two players to the school's roster, which will complete it at 105 players, per ESPN sources. This will lock LSU's roster for the rest of the year, which will eliminate the program's ability to add Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris," Thamel wrote in a post on X.

This should seemingly bring the whole ordeal to a close.

title: LSU locks roster, Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris will not play for the Tigers
description: Wright and Harris were both on rosters during the NFL preseason, and their potential return to college football sparked plenty of controversy.
fullText:
The battle over former NFL players returning to college appears to be over, for now.

LSU has added two players to its roster, bringing the total to 105 players. The Tigers added DE Gabriel Reliford and CB Aidan Anding, per Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger.

With the roster at 105 players, neither Dae'Quan Wright nor Zxavian Harris will be allowed to join the LSU roster this season.

Wright and Harris have been in the media and the subject of plenty of discussion because both of them participated in this year's NFL preseason, going so far as to suit up for preseason games.

After not making their respective NFL rosters, and after the NCAA passed a new eligibility rule allowing players five years of eligibility over five years, both Wright and Harris were looking to return to the college ranks for one more season.

Lawyers got involved, and different injunctions were permitted in different states, and the situation got extremely confusing and murky very quickly.

This sparked plenty of controversy among FBS teams, culminating in the SEC and LSU scheduling court dates and meetings to discuss what could be done to the school should it add pro players. One outcome included the conference removing LSU as a member school, but that may have been avoided.

While this seems like it was a big threat from the SEC, Dellenger reported that if the vote had passed and been enacted immediately, next week's highly anticipated game between Ole Miss and LSU would have suddenly been a non-conference game.

At this time, it has not been reported whether Thursday's scheduled meeting to "decide whether to terminate Louisiana State University ('LSU') as an SEC member institution" has been canceled or if it will still be held.

Wright and Harris were ruled eligible ahead of LSU's season-opening game against Clemson. Both players were with new head coach Lane Kiffin at Ole Miss, but Kiffin opted not to add them to the roster at the time, leaving two spots open out of a maximum of 105.

The LSU head coach spoke about the decision during an appearance on "College GameDay," mainly attributing it to the fact that they didn't yet know what a punishment, if any, would look like for the program.

"That wasn't easy. As much as I feel for the players, and I believe that you fight for what you believe in, and I believe that, you know, these kids have an opportunity to play, just like all of the other kids around the country that are winning court cases and being put on rosters.

But the same time, I'm the head coach at LSU and I had to make a decision that is for the big picture of LSU and the LSU football program, with the uncertainties of what potentially could've come by adding them to the roster."

"That wasn't easy. As much as I feel for the players ... I had to make a decision that is for the big picture of LSU."

Lane Kiffin on the decision to not roster Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris for today's game against Clemson. pic.twitter.com/iPVHJTYoav

Now with its roster officially set, LSU will look to continue the momentum generated with a Week 1 dominant 51-10 win over Clemson.

title: Space Force Uniform Is Inspired by Quasi-Satirical Film 'Starship Troopers'
description: The president shared photos on Truth Social of the uniforms, which include in their color palette "space gray" and "midnight black" as well as knee-high leather boots
fullText:
Among a flurry of posts this weekend, Donald Trump revealed the service dress uniform designs for his Space Force.

Without additional comment, the president shared photos and an overview of the uniforms on Truth Social, which include in their color palette “space gray” and “midnight black” as well as knee high leather boots and snazzy epaulettes. The overview indicated the ensemble was “inspired by the discipline and functionality of the Starship Trooper uniform.”

The admission is a bit of a shocker, not just because Trump loves winners and the critically-panned 1997 Paul Verhoeven film was a flop, but also because it was a satire of fascism. In his review at the time, Roger Ebert noted the picture’s “quasi-fascist militarism,” while admitting that those aspects were leavened a bit by “an element of sly satire.” But, for Ebert, that was not enough. “We smile at the satirical asides, but where’s the warmth of human nature? The spark of genius or rebellion? If Star Wars is humanist, Starship Troopers is totalitarian.”

As for the costumes themselves, Ebert was only slightly less critical. He calls them “a cross between Buck Rogers and the Archie comic books.”

Trump has seemingly drawn inspiration from movies and television before for his newest branch of the United States Armed Forces, which he created in 2019. When the president unveiled the logo, science fiction fans almost immediately called out the similarity to that worn by Captain Kirk and other Starfleet officers in Gene Roddenberry’s enduring, space faring sci-fi franchise. Star Trek legend George Takei even weighed in, telling Trump to give the source material its due.

In 2020, then-Vice President Mike Pence celebrated the one year anniversary of Trump’s new branch by announcing that — as those serving in the Navy are known as sailors and those in the army are known as soldiers — “henceforth, the members of the United States Space Force will be known as ‘guardians.’”

The announcement drew a quick reaction from Guardians of the Galaxy fans, who thought there might be an unacknowledged connection between the film series and the new name.

title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1M
description: Singapore's prime minister Lawrence Wong will see his annual pay rise to 3.6 million Singapore dollars ($2.8m; £2.1m).
fullText:
Singapore's government says it will raise the annual salaries of its ministers and other office holders, including its prime minister who is the highest paid political leader in the world.

Lawrence Wong will see an increase of 1.4 million Singapore dollars ($1.1m; £818,000) in his annual pay package. He has said he will donate this pay increase to charity over the next five years.

Wong said that raising the pay of ministers was necessary to attract better talent. The government has previously argued that paying ministers high salaries deters corruption.

But the move has attracted criticism in Singapore where there is deep concern about job security and the rising cost of living.

Even before his pay raise kicks in, Wong is still by far the highest paid world leader.

He currently receives an annual salary of S$2.2m and will now see his pay go up by more than 60% to S$3.6m ($2.8m).

Next is Hong Kong chief executive John Lee, who earns about $719,000, followed by Switzerland's president Guy Parmelin with $606,000.

US president Donald Trump earns $400,000 a year, while British PM Andy Burnham takes in $230,000.

On Tuesday, Wong acknowledged that Singapore ministers' salaries have attracted scrutiny given that they were much more than what most citizens earn. The median monthly income in the country is S$5,775.

But he argued that he has faced difficulty convincing business leaders and top civil servants to run for political office.

While the government cannot match what some of these people earn, "we do not make the financial hurdle unnecessarily high" for them to give up their careers and join politics, he said.

"Overall, I believe this will give me and future prime ministers a better chance of persuading capable Singaporeans to step forward, and of building the strongest possible team for Singapore," he said.

Currently, the base pay package of ministers is about S$1.1m. With the new pay scheme, that will increase to around S$1.2m.

But Wong said he expects most of these ministers to receive even more than that - around S$1.35m - by the end of the current term of government, as pay will increase based on performance.

Part of their pay package is determined by whether the country reaches certain targets for unemployment rate, income growth, and GDP growth.

The topic of high salaries for Singapore's ministers has long been a lightning rod of criticism for the ruling People's Action Party (PAP), which has led the country since independence.

In a landmark general election in 2011 the PAP saw its lowest vote share in decades, fuelled partly by voters' unhappiness over ministers' pay as well as immigration policies. The following year, the government slashed ministers' salaries.

Wong's predecessor, Lee Hsien Loong, had also pledged to donate his salary increase to charity for several years back in 2007.

The government has for years pointed to its lack of corruption - Singapore consistently ranks near the top of Transparency International's annual Corruption Perceptions Index - as proof that the ministerial pay system works, arguing that it reduces the temptation for ministers to accept bribes.

But in a country where the average income is far below such sums, the issue continues to rankle and the latest announcement is no exception.

On Tuesday many online posted comments critical of the pay raise, saying it was "tone deaf" given current concerns about retrenchments, jobs for fresh graduates and inflation.

Retrenchments in Singapore hit their highest level in more than five years in the last quarter, according to government figures.

But there were a few who agreed with the move, saying it was necessary to have "the best of the best" running the country.

title: We analyzed 2026 WhatsApp rates in 40 countries and built a calculator
description: Official WhatsApp Business API pricing for 40+ countries. Compare Meta rates vs BSP markups.
fullText:
Compare Meta official rates vs average provider rates (15-25% markup)

Browse country-specific rate breakdowns and BSP comparisons for 20+ markets.

WhatsApp Business API cost depends on country and category. Example current Meta rates include US marketing USD 0.025; Brazil marketing USD 0.0625.

WhatsApp Business API is not completely free. Service conversations inside the 24-hour customer service window can be free, while marketing, utility, and authentication messages are paid according to Meta's country-specific rate card.

Meta groups WhatsApp Business messages into marketing, utility, authentication, and service categories. Marketing is used for promotions, utility for transactional updates, authentication for one-time passwords, and service for customer support conversations.

Many Business Solution Providers add a markup on top of Meta's official WhatsApp rates. This calculator shows the typical 15-25% BSP markup range so teams can compare the direct Meta rate with provider pricing.

WhatsApp Business pricing is based on billable business conversations and message categories, but teams often compare costs as an effective per message rate for planning and provider audits.

The rate comparisons are generated from the application's current Meta rate database and use Decimal arithmetic for currency amounts. When the database is updated, the homepage and country FAQ copy can reflect those current rates.

Some markets use local-currency billing. Brazil is represented in the current database with AUD rates, India is commonly billed in INR, and many other countries are shown in USD.

WhatsApp Business API pricing is built around conversation-based billing rather than a simple monthly subscription. A conversation is a 24-hour billing window opened when either the business or the customer sends the first qualifying message. During that window, the business can exchange messages with the same customer without opening a second charge in the same category. This is why the headline WhatsApp cost per message can be confusing: many pricing tables show a unit rate because it is easy to compare countries and categories, but the underlying billing event is the conversation window. The calculator above keeps the comparison practical by multiplying the current Meta rate by your planned volume, then showing how a typical provider markup changes the total. That makes WhatsApp API pricing easier to budget before you connect a CRM, support inbox, or marketing automation platform.

Country matters as much as category. Meta publishes different official rates for different destination markets, so a campaign sent to the United States will not necessarily cost the same as a campaign sent to Brazil, India, Indonesia, or Mexico. Currency also matters because many finance teams plan in USD even when the local market is billed in BRL, INR, or another currency. This page uses the rate data stored in the application database and converts totals through the same billing logic as the calculator, so the examples are tied to real pricing records instead of static copy. If your team is comparing WhatsApp Business pricing across vendors, always separate the official Meta component from the provider fee before deciding whether a quote is expensive.

Meta groups WhatsApp Business conversations into four categories: marketing, utility, authentication, and service. Marketing conversations are generally the most expensive because they include promotional campaigns, product launches, win-back offers, newsletters, and other business-initiated messages designed to drive revenue. Utility conversations cover operational updates such as order confirmations, appointment reminders, shipping alerts, account notices, and receipts. Authentication conversations are used for one-time passcodes, login verification, and security checks. Service conversations are customer-initiated support interactions, where the user contacts the business first and the business replies inside the customer service window.

The category determines the WhatsApp business message cost more than the template length or the number of words in the message. A short promotional coupon is still marketing, while a longer order-status update can still be utility if it is transactional and expected by the user. This classification matters because using the wrong template category can distort your forecast and may create compliance problems during template review. For planning, treat marketing as the budget-sensitive category, utility as the operational category, authentication as the security category, and service as the support category. Teams that understand these boundaries can forecast monthly spend more accurately and avoid comparing a marketing campaign quote against a utility notification rate.

Most businesses do not access the WhatsApp Business API directly. They work through a Business Solution Provider, often called a BSP, such as Twilio, MessageBird, 360dialog, WATI, or another regional provider. The BSP connects your application to WhatsApp, hosts messaging infrastructure, manages webhooks, provides dashboards, and often adds support tooling, template submission workflows, delivery reporting, and compliance guidance. In exchange, providers commonly add a 15-25% markup on top of Meta's official rates, sometimes bundled with platform fees, inbox seats, automation features, or minimum monthly commitments.

That markup is not automatically bad. If the provider reduces engineering time, improves deliverability visibility, or gives your support and marketing teams a usable interface, the extra cost may be cheaper than building and maintaining the integration yourself. The problem is opacity: many invoices blend the official Meta fee with the BSP fee, which makes it hard to know whether your WhatsApp Business API pricing is driven by message volume, destination country, category mix, or vendor margin. The most useful comparison is the one this calculator makes: official Meta total beside a provider-adjusted total. Once those numbers are separated, procurement can negotiate markup, engineering can evaluate direct integration, and growth teams can decide whether a campaign still has healthy unit economics.

Sending 1,000 marketing messages to US customers costs approximately $25.0000 at Meta's official rate, or $30.0000 with a typical BSP. That is a difference of $5.0000 per thousand marketing conversations before any separate platform subscription or seat fee is added. For a small campaign this gap may look modest, but at tens or hundreds of thousands of sends it becomes a real line item in the marketing budget.

For Brazil marketing traffic, the same 1,000-message planning scenario is $62.5000 at the official Meta rate and $75.0000 through a typical marked-up provider, leaving $12.5000 in avoidable markup for every thousand messages. Brazil is a good example of why country-level WhatsApp API pricing matters: a global average can hide the markets where campaigns are profitable and the markets where markup erodes contribution margin.

Utility notifications in India show a different cost profile. Sending 1,000 utility messages is approximately $1.4000 at Meta's official rate, compared with $1.6800 after a typical BSP markup. The markup difference is $0.2800 per thousand messages. Because utility traffic often scales with orders, bookings, deliveries, and account activity, even a low WhatsApp cost per message can become material when the business sends millions of operational notifications each month.

These examples are intentionally narrow: one country, one category, one volume, and one target currency at a time. Real invoices are usually a blend of marketing blasts, lifecycle utility messages, login verification, and customer support. To estimate a full month, model each traffic stream separately, apply the right destination country and category, then add the totals. That approach is more accurate than multiplying one blended rate across all messages, because the rate mix changes whenever your campaign calendar, customer geography, or support volume changes.

A common source of confusion is the difference between conversation billing and per-message planning. Meta bills around conversation windows, but businesses often forecast by message count because campaign tools, CRMs, and data warehouses track sends, deliveries, and replies as message events. When someone asks for the WhatsApp cost per message, they usually want a practical unit cost for budgeting rather than a statement about the exact billing primitive. This calculator uses per-message-style volume inputs so teams can compare Meta rates and provider rates quickly, while still explaining that the billed unit is tied to the conversation category and 24-hour window.

The distinction matters most when a customer sends multiple replies or when a business sends several follow-up messages inside the same open conversation. Those extra interactions may not create a new charge if they stay within the active window and category rules. On the other hand, starting a new business-initiated conversation after the window closes can create a new billable event. For forecasting, use message volume as a simple first-pass model, then refine it with your actual conversation open rates, reply rates, and support patterns once you have production data.

WhatsApp also includes free or lower-cost situations that can change the final invoice. When a customer messages your business first, you can respond inside the customer service window without treating every reply like a new outbound marketing push. Entry points from Facebook or Instagram ads can also create free messaging windows for eligible ad-to-WhatsApp conversations. These rules are valuable for support and acquisition teams because they reward conversations that begin with user intent. They do not eliminate the need to understand WhatsApp Business API pricing, but they do mean that two companies with the same total message count can pay different amounts depending on who initiated the conversation and how quickly the business replied.

The fastest way to reduce cost is to make your category mix honest and intentional. Do not send promotional content as utility, but do avoid classifying operational messages as marketing just because the template was written by a growth team. Next, negotiate BSP markup once you know your official Meta baseline; a provider is easier to evaluate when you can show the exact difference between official rates and marked-up rates. Third, batch and target marketing campaigns carefully. Sending fewer, better-segmented promotions often improves return on spend more than chasing the cheapest provider. Fourth, monitor country-level rate changes because a campaign that works in one market may not work in another. Finally, review invoices for platform fees, minimums, failed-message policies, and currency conversion spreads, since the visible WhatsApp business message cost is only one part of the total vendor bill.

For teams that send at scale, the right operating rhythm is monthly. Export your actual sends by country and category, compare the official Meta component with the provider component, and update your forecast before the next campaign calendar is approved. If the provider markup is small and the tooling saves time, keep it. If the markup grows faster than the value of the tooling, consider renegotiating, switching BSPs, or moving some traffic closer to Meta's official API. The goal is not always to pay the absolute lowest rate; it is to know exactly what you are paying for and whether that cost supports the customer experience and revenue outcome you expect.

title: Apple iPod Engraver (2019)
description: Making the iPod engraver page for Apple’s online store
fullText:
I spent 2004–2006 working at Apple as a UI engineer for their online store. Part of my job was to prototype concepts that would add some interactive sparkle to the site.

One such project improved the “Personalize your iPod” page, where customers could submit two lines of text to be engraved on the back of the iPod they were ordering.

As originally designed the page offered no interaction beyond a plain form. I added a rotatable iPod, a live “engraved” preview of the customer’s text, and a highlight of any change in shipping times.

I animated the iPod by cycling through a series of JPEGs using JavaScript. The engraving was created using imagemagick, which took the user’s text and returned an “engraved” image to be overlaid on the rear of the iPod. The shipping highlight was achieved by switching CSS classes to change the background color, in the style of a classic yellow fade.

There’s an old working demo if you’d like to try it yourself.

We obviously have much better ways of doing such things today, but in 2005, with limited browser technology, those solutions seemed a little bit magical.

fullText:
Company behind ChatGPT says 10,000 of its AI systems cracked the Navier-Stokes problem in 88 hours

OpenAI claims to have solved a major mathematics problem that has stumped humans for nearly a century after spending millions of dollars on the artificial intelligence-led endeavour.

The company behind ChatGPT said it had cracked the Navier-Stokes problem, one of seven Millennium Prize Problems published by the Clay Mathematics Institute to highlight some of the biggest unsolved puzzles in the field.

However, the announcement swiftly became mired in controversy after mathematician Tristan Buckmaster, a professor at New York University, said OpenAI accelerated its work on the problem after hearing that he and another researcher at Anthropic, an OpenAI rival, were poised to announce their own breakthrough.

Buckmaster had further concerns because the pair’s work in progress was stored in OpenAI’s Codex model, which is used for writing computer programs, potentially making the work visible to the OpenAI team.

In a document posted on his website, he added: “I do not know what their model did, or how. I do not know whether our data was used. I am not accusing anyone of anything.”

At a press briefing on Tuesday, OpenAI researcher Sebastien Bubeck denied that the company had used the pair’s work or accessed material shared with OpenAI’s servers.

OpenAI’s announcement on the breakthrough gave more details, saying that the company was inspired to launch the effort after hearing rumours that two Millennium Prize Problems had been solved. It also said it could not rule out that data from the pair’s use of their products “helped improve our models.”

OpenAI said it tackled the Navier-Stokes problem with an internal OpenAI system that was more powerful than its latest GPT-6 Astra model. About 10,000 AI agents – AI systems that carry out tasks autonomously – worked on the problem at once and reached the solution in 88 hours.

“A major goal of our work is to empower scientists to advance research and technology that benefits all of humanity,” OpenAI researchers wrote in a blog. “We believe it is important to inform the world about the pace of AI progress and what to expect from upcoming models”.

The breakthrough is the latest to demonstrate how advanced artificial intelligence models consuming enormous amounts of computing power are encroaching on and reshaping the field of mathematics. In May, OpenAI claimed progress in another mathematical problem first proposed 80 years ago, while Google DeepMind has also claimed maths achievements with its models.

Bubeck said the solution to the Navier-Stokes problem was “a spectacular culmination of the arc we have seen over the past 12 months”.

The Navier-Stokes problem asks whether equations that are used to describe the movement of fluids like air and water fail under particular conditions. OpenAI’s proof suggests that they do, with the equations occasionally “blowing up” with the speed of fluids becoming impossibly infinite. It took OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra about 17 hours to verify the solution.

Mathematicians who solve any of the Millennium Prize Problems are in line for a $1m (£740,000) reward from the Clay Mathematics Institute. OpenAI, which is preparing for a flotation that could value the business at around $1tn, said it did not intend to claim the prize.

The clash with Buckmaster aside, the maths announcement also allows OpenAI to cast its technology in a positive light after a period of alarm over how safely it is being developed. OpenAI revealed in July that a swarm of agents had hacked into Hugging Face, a third'-party software store, during a cybersecurity test.

The incident, plus a similar episode at Anthropic, has led to renewed calls for curbs on AI development, with US senators calling last week for a permanent ban of AI “superintelligence” – the term for systems that outperform humans in all cognitive tasks.

title: Former Colorado crime analyst gets 10-year prison sentence for manipulating DNA data
description: A judge sentenced a former forensic analyst for the Colorado Bureau of Investigation to 10 years in prison on Tuesday after authorities said her manipulation of DNA data raised questions about the val...
fullText:
GOLDEN, Colo. (AP) — A judge sentenced a former forensic analyst for the Colorado Bureau of Investigation to 10 years in prison on Tuesday after authorities said her manipulation of DNA data raised questions about the validity of hundreds of criminal cases.

Yvonne "Missy" Woods pleaded guilty in June to perjury, attempting to influence a public servant, forgery and committing a cybercrime. Dozens of other counts were dismissed as part of a plea agreement.

Problems with the scientist's work were found in cases involving homicide, sexual assault, robbery and other crimes, according to authorities. Prosecutors were forced to review hundreds of cases, and at least one murder conviction was vacated as a result of Woods' misconduct.

Woods had faced between 8 and 16 years in prison during Tuesday's sentencing hearing before state District Judge Andrew Poland in Golden, Colorado.

She resigned in 2023 after a decades-long career. Authorities accused her of altering data to conceal tampering, deleting data that showed she failed to troubleshoot issues within the testing process and not thoroughly documenting tests performed in case records.

Woods apologized during Tuesday's hearing but said she knew saying sorry would not undo the harm she caused, the Denver Post reported.

"For many years I was entrusted with evidence that could have profound consequences for defendants, victims, families and the courts. I failed that responsibility. I am deeply sorry for that failure," she said.

Following the sentencing, Colorado Bureau of Investigation officials said they have sought to reform their laboratories in response to the data scandal as they try to rebuild public trust.

"The actions of one individual never define this organization, and they do not define the dedicated public servants who continued showing up every day with integrity," bureau Director Armando Saldate said in a statement.

The investigation into Woods' misconduct began in September 2023 after an intern at the bureau discovered missing information in a case that Woods handled in 2018. According to an arrest affidavit, Woods allegedly told investigators at one point that she had changed data to complete cases more quickly.

In the vacated murder case, Michael Clark was released from prison in 2025 after his lawyers argued that DNA evidence was mishandled by Woods. Prosecutors said they would seek to retry him.

In two homicide cases, the defendants received lesser sentences under plea deals than they could have faced if they went to trial because prosecutors were afraid Woods' involvement could lead to acquittals.

Convictions in other cases also have been challenged in courts across Colorado.

A Colorado Bureau of Investigation internal affairs report in 2024 revealed that concerns about Woods' work first surfaced more than a decade ago. As early as 2014, a worker questioned her testing of evidence, and in 2018 she was temporarily removed from working on DNA cases after being accused of data manipulation, the report said.

State officials have said that the response to Woods' actions could end up costing more than $11 million.

title: Ballots discounted for late postmarks surged in Washington and Oregon after Postal Service changes
description: The number of ballots rejected for late postmarks has soared in the vote-by-mail states of Washington and Oregon, according to newly released data highlighting concerns about recent changes in U.S. Po...
fullText:
SEATTLE (AP) — The number of ballots rejected for late postmarks has soared in the vote-by-mail states of Washington and Oregon, according to newly released data highlighting concerns about recent changes in U.S. Postal Service operations ahead of this fall's pivotal midterm election.

The struggling agency has been consolidating its operations with an emphasis on regional hubs in an effort to save billions of dollars. Some U.S. senators and election officials for months have been warning that the changes could delay the application of postmarks to ballots — even if they're mailed on or before Election Day. That would prevent otherwise valid votes from counting.

That prediction is being borne out, they say, with thousands of voters having their ballots rejected during this year's primaries.

"More Oregonians had their voices go unheard just because their ballots couldn't make it through the mail in time," Oregon Secretary of State Tobias Read told a news conference Tuesday, referring to the state's primary in May. "That is unacceptable."

The operational changes at the Postal Service are compounding worries about the future of voting by mail, especially in some Western states where the method is universal and widely popular. Trump has repeatedly attacked mail-in voting, falsely claiming it's riddled with fraud, despite having voted by mail himself.

Over the weekend, his administration asked the U.S. Supreme Court to overturn a judge's ruling blocking his executive order that seeks to restrict mail-in voting, a method used by nearly one-third of voters in the U.S.

Read said he is asking lawmakers for emergency funding to install 20 new ballot drop boxes in areas where they're not otherwise easily accessible to voters. Washington's secretary of state this year has spent about $300,000 to reimburse counties for the addition of 21 drop boxes.

In two rural Washington counties — both of which have reliably backed President Donald Trump — ballots rejected for late postmarks represented more than 4% of all ballots cast in last month's primary. Democratic Sen. Maria Cantwell of Washington called it ironic that postal changes might disenfranchise some of Trump's most stable supporters.

"The Postal Service is disenfranchising voters across the United States with policies that are leaving them with a ballot that was cast, but never counted," she said.

In December, the Postal Service finalized a rule clarifying that postmarks don't necessarily reflect the date the agency first took possession of a piece of mail, but rather the day it was handled in one of its processing centers. Those processing centers are increasingly likely to be farther from certain communities due to recent consolidations.

And since last year, USPS policy has dictated that mail is transported once a day — rather than twice — from post offices or collection boxes that are more than 50 miles (80.47 kilometers) from a postal distribution center.

In a written statement, the Postal Service acknowledged that changes in how it transports mail could result in postmarking delays. It noted that anyone who wants to ensure their ballots are postmarked on time can go into a post office and ask for it to be stamped manually, free of charge.

"Our consistent message to voters who choose to vote by mail is to mail early" — at least one week before ballots are due, the statement said.

Some 7,314 ballots that arrived in the mail during Oregon's weeklong grace period for this year's May primary were not counted because they were postmarked after Election Day — a rejection rate of 13%, up from 9.5% two years earlier, Read said.

In Washington, the number of late-postmarked ballots first jumped last year, after postal changes had taken effect. Officials responded by urging people to get their ballots in early and by installing more drop boxes. Drop box use did increase in this year's primary, but the number of late-postmarked ballots was still a problem: 20,267 — up from 16,131 in 2024.

The data paralleled numbers in California, where during this year's June primary about 93,500 voters had their ballots rejected because they were postmarked or arrived too late to be counted.

In some rural Washington counties where voters often return ballots by mail because drop boxes are farther away, the data was most pronounced. In Stevens County in Washington's northeastern corner, the rate at which mailed ballots were rejected for late postmarks quadrupled.

Stevens County Auditor Lori Larsen said that on Aug. 7, three days after the primary and during the state's grace period for ballots to arrive, her office received a haul of 547 ballots with late postmarks. There were so many that she initially thought the mail must have been interrupted by wildfires in the region, but when she looked at the ZIP codes they originated from, she realized that wasn't the case.

"To me that is a number that suggests that many, if not all, of those folks thought they were timely delivering their ballot into USPS custody," Larsen said in a phone interview.

Her office is now rushing to double the number of secure ballot drop boxes in the county from five to 10.

In conservative Yakima County, where nearly 4.4% of all ballots cast in the primary were rejected for late postmarks, local mail is now sent to a processing center in Spokane — about 200 miles (320 km) away — before being returned to Yakima, said county Auditor Charles Ross.

He said that while elections officials try to treat all voters equally, the postal changes could make it more likely that those in rural areas won't have their vote counted.

"If you're in one of these rural areas like where we live and you put your ballot in the post office box three days before the election, and if you live in Seattle or Spokane and you put your ballot in the same blue box three days before the election — there's a high likelihood that those two ballots are going to be treated differently," Ross said.

title: Over 1,500 pounds of pork recalled. See affected products
description: Over 1,500 pounds of imported, ready-to-eat pork products distributed to eight states have been recalled. See the affected products.
fullText:
More than 1,500 pounds of imported, ready-to-eat pork products are being recalled due to potential listeria contamination, the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service announced on Sunday, Sept. 6.

The pork was produced at Est. 1937L Bome SRL in Italy on May 21, 2026, and imported on various dates within July 2026, according to the FSIS. Prime Line Distributors Inc., from Fort Lauderdale, Florida, and Ferrarini USA Inc., from Hoboken, New Jersey, distributed the affected products.

The recall was classified as a Class I, which the USDA describes as a health hazard situation where there is a "reasonable probability that the use of the product will cause serious, adverse health consequences or death."

Here's what else to know about the recall.

The following products are subject to the recall, according to the FSIS:

Various weight cardboard cases containing two pieces of individually vacuum-packed "PRIME LINE DISTRIBUTORS, INC. GUANCIALE PORK JOWL PRODUCT OF ITALY" with "LOT: 263311US" and "BEST IF USE BY DATE: 05.16.27" printed on the label.

Various weights individually vacuum-packaged "GUANCIALE PORK JOWL PRODUCT OF ITALY" with "LOT: 263311US" and "BEST IF USE BY: 05.16.27" printed on the label. The product has an additional label with "DOK GUANCIALE" on the packaging.

Various weight cardboard cases containing two pieces of individually vacuum-packed "GUANCIALE PORK JOWL PRODUCT OF ITALY" with "LOT: 263311US" and "BEST IF USE BY DATE: 05.16.27" printed on the label.

Various weights individually vacuum-packaged "FERRARINI GUANCIALE DRY-CURED PORK JOWL" with "LOT: 263311US" and "BEST IF USE BY DATE: 05.16.27" printed on the label.

The FSIS said the products subject to recall bear establishment number "IT 1937 L CE" inside the Italian mark of inspection or printed on the case label.

Prime Line Distributors' products were shipped to distributors and food service locations in Florida, and Ferrarini USA's items were shipped to distributors and food service locations in California, Florida, Idaho, Illinois, Michigan, New Jersey, New York and Texas.

According to the FSIS, there have been no confirmed reports of illness from consuming these products. Anyone concerned about an illness should contact a health care provider.

Food service and retail locations are urged not to serve or sell these products. The FSIS says to throw the products away or return them to the place of purchase.

Consuming food contaminated with listeria can cause listeriosis, a serious infection that primarily affects older adults, people with weakened immune systems and pregnant women and their newborns. Less commonly, people outside these risk groups are affected.

Listeriosis can cause fever, muscle aches, headache, stiff neck, confusion, loss of balance and convulsions, sometimes preceded by diarrhea or other gastrointestinal symptoms, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. An invasive infection spreads beyond the infected person's gastrointestinal tract.

In pregnant women, the infection can cause miscarriages, stillbirths, premature delivery or life-threatening infection of the newborn. In addition, serious and sometimes fatal infections can occur in older adults and individuals with weakened immune systems. Listeriosis is often treated with antibiotics.

title: Judge revives GOP Missouri congressional map after Kavanaugh denies Republican appeal
description: The issue is likely to return to the Supreme Court as soon as Wednesday.
fullText:
Shortly after Supreme Court Justice Brett Kavanaugh declined to intervene in the dispute over Missouri's congressional map -- leaving in place a state court mandate that officials use a map favored by Democrats -- a federal district court judge issued an opposing decision that the GOP-preferred map should stand, at least for now.

"Using a different map for the general election would wreak havoc on the fairness and orderliness of Missouri's congressional elections, calling into question the candidacy of those nominated in the primaries and the votes of those who voted in the primaries. Widespread voter confusion would inevitably follow," Judge Stephen Clark wrote.

The legal whiplash injected fresh confusion as both parties continue to wrangle over a mid-decade redistricting push and state election administrators scramble to prepare ballots for the November election.

The bottom line at the moment is that the standoff over Missouri's U.S. House districts remains unresolved and is likely to return to the Supreme Court, possibly as soon as Wednesday.

'Democrats are on offense': House Dems' campaign arm adds 5 seats to target list

It's the latest twist in Missouri's unprecedented fight over redistricting that has stretched past the deadline by which candidates and voters typically settle in for the fall campaign.

The state's Republican-controlled legislature last year passed into law a new congressional map that redrew the district currently held by Democratic U.S. Rep. Emanuel Cleaver to lean Republican as part of a nationwide mid-decade redistricting push encouraged by President Donald Trump.

But Democrats and other opponents of the new map filed legal challenges and began a ballot initiative to put the new map up for a vote in November, allowing voters to potentially decide whether to keep the map in place. They also argued that if the new map was put up for a referendum vote in November, that would suspend the law establishing the new map unless voters approved it and that Missouri's elections should be held under the state's older congressional map.

Missouri Secretary of State Denny Hoskins initially decided in early August that he would not certify the referendum to the ballot, saying he had determined it was unconstitutional. The group pushing the referendum vote, People Not Politicians, successfully appealed that ruling to the state Supreme Court, which ruled to block the new map from being used in November and to allow the ballot initiative to proceed.

Sen. Warnock urges Democrats to investigate officials who redrew maps

Republicans appealed to the U.S. Supreme Court seeking intervention as they simultaneously pursued a second-track legal front.

Kavanaugh, who oversees Missouri federal courts, declined Republicans' emergency appeal in one case on Wednesday without explanation.  Moments later Judge Clark issued his ruling in a separate case, which acknowledged Kavanaugh's decision.

Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway on Tuesday evening indicated the state will be ready to use the newer 2025 map after Clark's ruling.

"Missouri is prepared to follow and comply with Chief Judge Clark's order that binds the state to using the [2025] Missouri FIRST map for the November General Election. We maintain that changing the congressional map in between the primary and general elections is simply not feasible and profoundly unjust to Missouri voters," she posted on X.

title: Hospital sorry after patient's nil-by-mouth death
description: Jacqueline Frehe, 97, was nil-by-mouth at the hospital - but was given food and later died.
fullText:
A healthcare trust says it has changed its guidelines after a 97-year-old woman was given food when she was nil-by-mouth, which led to her death.

Coroner for Somerset Vanessa McKinlay wrote a prevention of future deaths report following the inquest into the death of Jacqueline Frehe, who died at Yeovil District Hospital in Somerset.

The inquest heard that when she was transferred from A&E to another ward, the staff there were not made aware that she was nil-by-mouth.

Somerset NHS Foundation Trust said it extended its "deepest sympathies" and apologised to Frehe's family and explained it was taking action on the coroner's findings.

The report said Frehe had been given food and drink on 25 August 2025.

It added this led to her vomiting and her condition "deteriorating significantly" until she died in hospital the same day.

The coroner said not only was the nil-by-mouth order not communicated between wards, but when Frehe's family mentioned her nil-by-mouth status, this was not documented by ward staff.

Somerset NHS Foundation Trust has since said it will improve its standardisation of emergency department-to-ward handover, how staff document, escalate, and act upon concerns raised by families, and will strengthen its education and training for clinical staff in relation to dysphagia [difficulty or discomfort when swallowing foods and liquids], aspiration risk, and safe management of nutrition and hydration.

Prof Deirdre Fowler, chief nurse and midwife at Somerset NHS Foundation Trust, said they had "carefully considered" the coroner's findings.

"We extend our deepest sympathies to Mrs Frehe's family at this very difficult time," she said.

"We recognise that opportunities were missed to ensure important information about her care was consistently communicated and acted upon, and we are sorry for this.

title: 4 family members killed in Bahamas small plane crash identified
description: Two grandparents and two grandchildren were aboard the plane, the family said.
fullText:
The bodies of four family members from Miami were recovered Tuesday following a small plane crash near the Bahamas, family members said.

A family statement provided to ABC News identified the passengers as Mario Lamar Sr., 80, and Lili Lamar, 79, and their grandchildren Sofi Sosa, 28, and Christian Sosa, 22. Mario Lamar was "an experienced pilot with more than 40 years of flying experience," according to the family.

"Our relatives ultimately located our loved ones and had to bring them aboard their own vessels," the family said in a statement Tuesday.

The cause of the crash is still under investigation, according to the Aircraft Accident Investigation Authority (AAIA) of The Bahamas. The agency said as of Tuesday afternoon it has not found the plane or any wreckage.

Around 2 p.m. on Monday, "the Royal Bahamian Defense Force requested Coast Guard assistance following a report of a downed airplane with four people aboard approximately 15 miles off Andros Island, Bahamas," the Coast Guard said.

The Bahamas Police Department identified the plane as a PA-34 Piper five-seater aircraft. It took off from Great Harbour Cay around 11:12 a.m. Monday and was bound for Miami Executive Airport, officials said.

"Air Traffic Control subsequently lost contact with the aircraft approximately 13 miles west of Andros Island," Bahamas Police said, adding that poor weather had postponed the search.

The investigation into the crash is ongoing, officials said. The family said it is asking for privacy.

"We are deeply grateful to everyone who supported us, searched alongside us, and kept our family in their prayers," they said in a statement.

title: The US Army is testing whether reserve drill sergeants could help train a larger force for a major war
description: The Army tested whether reserve drill sergeants could help expand boot camp during a major conflict without lowering basic training standards.
fullText:
The Army is planning for a potential future fight that could require it to train more recruits quickly.

The service recently examined how reservists could help rapidly plus-up basic training.

The experiment will be used as a springboard for a larger effort next year.

The US Army is testing whether it could use reserve drill sergeants and other personnel to quickly expand basic training in the event that a major conflict suddenly needed training pipelines to produce far more soldiers.

An experiment called Operation Wildcat Rising put dozens of Army Reserve drill sergeants into a single basic training cycle at Fort Sill, Oklahoma, this summer to examine how the Army might increase its existing training capacity while also maintaining basic training standards.

While the reserve already helps reinforce the Army's training base, its drill sergeants have previously been distributed individually to fill gaps in active units, the Army said in a news release. Wildcat Rising tested a different wartime model and gave a reserve formation under its own leadership a larger share of the training mission.

"Our drill sergeants told us this experience was worth several traditional rotations," Col. Matthew Horning, the commander of 1st Brigade, 95th Training Division, and one of the officials who oversaw the experiment, said in the release.

"Now we take what we learned, give our formations the preparation time they need and refine the model for the next phase," he said.

In a large-scale conflict, the military may be forced to grow its ranks on a scale not seen in decades, potentially putting serious pressure on the bases, instructors, and other resources involved in transforming civilians into soldiers. Because of that, Army officials want to assess how reserve troops might help that formative training in a time of crisis.

"At the end of the day, we have to train these men and women for combat," Maj. Gen. Michael Dougherty, commander of the 80th Training Command, said in the release. "Basic Combat Training is step one, and we have to get that right."

Training recruits is a notoriously grueling task that can be assigned to troops in nearly any military job. The work comes with long hours, little sleep, constant responsibility for recruit safety, and the relentless physical and emotional strain of overseeing basic training.

A post-training review highlighted the challenges ahead as the Army looks to scale. Some reservists arrived at Fort Sill lacking required certifications for their new roles, and communications failures left others unclear about the requirements before they arrived, the Army said. Tight rotation timelines also left little time for teams to exchange insight as they arrived and departed.

Army officials said encountering those obstacles this time will help it shape a larger follow-on brigade-level effort next year.

title: Fetterman leans on unlikely GOP ally as Dems sharpen their knives over explosive report

fullText:
Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., is under fire over leaked texts with his staff in which he brushed off meetings with a children's hospital and paralyzed veterans, but he is pushing back, calling the reports "smears" with support from his Republican Pennsylvania colleague, Sen. Dave McCormick.

Fetterman broke his silence following a bombshell report based on leaked text messages between him and his staff that portrayed him as brushing off basic duties of being a senator, including meetings with constituents.

Fetterman told CNN in a statement that "disgruntled" staffers had concocted the story, first reported by the Wall Street Journal, to knock his reputation.

Fetterman Faces Dem Revolt As Bombshell Report Fuels Push To Oust Him: 'Disgrace'

"Per usual — lies, half-truths, innuendos, smears and anonymous," Fetterman said.

"No matter how many smears or stories, I'm proud to continue to deliver for Pennsylvania," he continued.

The lawmaker's response follows an explosive report published last week that painted Fetterman as a politician more interested in appearing on Fox News to discuss Israel than meeting with constituents, including a group of paralyzed veterans from his state, and opting to blow off a funeral for slain police officers because it would have taken too long.

While other Democratic members of the Pennsylvania delegation were furious with Fetterman, his fellow senator, McCormick, came to his defense.

"These stories are the latest example of outrageously disloyal staff and forces on the Left using anonymous leaks to cancel my friend John Fetterman," McCormick said on X. "They hate that he is an independent thinker who refuses to fall into line so they want to silence him."

Why Trump, Gop Are Courting John Fetterman, Who Insists He'll Remain A Democrat

Fetterman and McCormick share a unique relationship in a Congress that has grown increasingly partisan. They're one of three Senate duos from a purple state, and Fetterman has vowed to not support an opponent when and if McCormick runs for re-election in 2030.

"Well, I would absolutely never move against my friend," Fetterman told reporters.

They also launched a joint fundraising effort in July, called Common Ground PA, according to federal financial filings.

Dnc Vice Chair Attacks Democratic Sen. John Fetterman: 'You're A Mess'

And the pair spent Labor Day together, per a post from McCormick, where they toured Bell & Evans, a chicken processing company in Pennsylvania.

"He and I will continue to work together to deliver for Pennsylvania by saving jobs at US Steel, passing a new law to make housing more affordable, securing $600 million to replace the Delaware River Bridge, and delivering critical funding to protect Presque Isle State Park," McCormick continued.

Still, members of the Pennsylvania delegation and beyond, including the vice chair of the Democratic National Committee, are laying the groundwork to oust him.

Rep. Chris Deluzio, D-Pa., a progressive representing southwest Pennsylvania, charged that Fetterman's behavior was "pathetic," and said that "this man has no sense of duty."

Whether Fetterman mount a bid for re-election in 2028 remains to be seen.

"He is not up for the high office he was elected to — and we in Pennsylvania will do something about it in 2028," Deluzio said on X.
